facts.statement: The type specimen of Eolambia was discovered by Carole and Ramal Jones in 1993.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Eolambia was discovered by Carole and Ramal Jones in 1993

facts.statement: All known specimens of Eolambia have been found in Emery County, Utah, within the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
facts.quote: All of the specimens have thus far been found in Emery County, Utah, in a layer of rock known as the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.

facts.statement: Eolambia could measure up to 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Measuring up to 6 m long, Eolambia is a large member of its group.

facts.statement: Eolambia lived in humid floodplain forests near lakes and ate gymnosperms, ferns, and flowering plants.
facts.quote: Eolambia would have lived in a forested environment at the edge of lakes in a humid floodplain environment, feeding on gymnosperms, ferns, and flowering plants.

facts.statement: Juvenile Eolambia were preyed upon by large crocodylomorphs living in lake waters.
facts.quote: As a juvenile, Eolambia would have been preyed upon by large crocodylomorphs residing in the lake waters.

facts.statement: Mature Eolambia individuals, at least eight to nine years old, were preyed upon by large theropods like Siats.
facts.quote: mature individuals (at least eight to nine years in age) were preyed on by large theropods such as the neovenatorid Siats.

facts.statement: In 1979, Peter Galton and James A. Jensen described a fragmentary femur (BYU 2000) of a hadrosaurian from the Cedar Mountain Formation in Arches National Park, Utah.
facts.quote: In 1979 Peter Galton and James A. Jensen described a fragmentary right femur, BYU 2000, belonging to a hadrosaurian dinosaur discovered in sediments belonging to the Cedar Mountain Formation in Arches National Park, Utah.

facts.statement: Carole Jones and Ramal Jones discovered fragmentary bones of Eolambia in 1993 at a site in the northwestern San Rafael Swell.
facts.quote: In 1993, Carole Jones and her husband Ramal Jones discovered fragmentary bones in a fossil site located in the northwestern region of the Swell.

facts.statement: Specimen CEUM 9758 represents partial remains of an adult hadrosauroid including skull parts, vertebrae, ischium, and leg.
facts.quote: The fossils, stored under the specimen number CEUM 9758, represent the partial remains of an adult hadrosauroid, including parts of the skull, vertebrae, ischium, and leg.

facts.statement: James Kirkland preliminarily described the Eolambia specimens in 1994 at a Society of Vertebrate Paleontology conference.
facts.quote: Kirkland went on to preliminarily describe the specimens in 1994 in a conference abstract at the annual meeting of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology.

facts.statement: James Kirkland formally named the genus Eolambia and its only species Eolambia caroljonesa in 1998.
facts.quote: In a 1998 paper published in the bulletin of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science, Kirkland formally named the specimens as a new genus, Eolambia, with the type and only species being Eolambia caroljonesa.

facts.statement: The genus name Eolambia combines the Greek word for dawn with a suffix derived from Lambeosaurus.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the Greek prefix eos/ἠώς ("dawn", "morning", implying "early") with the suffix lambia (derived from Lambeosaurus, which is in turn named after Canadian paleontologist Lawrence Lambe).

facts.statement: At least twelve individuals, including eight juveniles, were found in a quarry south of Emery, Utah.
facts.quote: At least twelve individuals, including at least eight juveniles, were discovered in a quarry south of the town of Emery, including parts from both the skull and the rest of the body.

facts.statement: Researchers caution that a specimen with an unusually deep dentary might represent a distinct hadrosauroid rather than Eolambia.
facts.quote: McDonald and colleagues cautioned that it may represent a distinct hadrosauroid that differs in the morphology of the dentary from Eolambia (albeit one that is not suggested by any of the other materials at the quarry).

facts.statement: Similarities between Eolambia and lambeosaurine hadrosaurids are considered either convergent evolution or misinterpretations.
facts.quote: Despite resembling hadrosaurids – lambeosaurine hadrosaurids in particular – in several features, leading to its initial identification as one of them, these similarities have been rejected as either entirely convergent or misinterpreted.

facts.statement: Eolambia may be more closely related to Protohadros, forming an isolated radiation of hadrosauroids based on skull and shoulder bone traits.
facts.quote: it may actually be more closely related to the North American Protohadros. This grouping, based on the straightness of the quadrate bone and scapula, would represent an isolated, endemic radiation of hadrosauroids.

facts.statement: Eolambia lived during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cenomanian,

facts.statement: J. Michael Parrish described various hadrosauroid teeth from the San Rafael Swell in 1991.
facts.quote: Various hadrosauroid teeth had also been found in quarries of small vertebrates in the western region of the San Rafael Swell, near Castle Dale in Emery County, Utah; they were described in 1991 by J. Michael Parrish.

facts.statement: Eolambia fossils are found exclusively in the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
facts.quote: All of the localities that Eolambia were discovered in belong to the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.

facts.statement: A 1997 study dated a volcanic ash layer in the formation containing Eolambia to 97 ± 0.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: A 1997 argon-argon dating of sanidine crystals recovered from a volcanic ash layer in the upper Cedar Mountain Formation by Cifelli and colleagues indicated an age of 97 ± 0.1 million years

facts.statement: Agreement between dating estimates indicates that Eolambia lived during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: At an approximate level, the Cifelli and Garrison estimates agree with each other, thus indicating a Cenomanian age for Eolambia.

facts.statement: Eolambia is classified as a large hadrosauroid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Eolambia is a large hadrosauroid.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2016 that Eolambia reached a body length of 6 meters and a weight of 1 metric ton.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated a body length of 6 m and a weight of 1 MT for Eolambia

facts.statement: An adult Eolambia specimen was estimated in 2008 to be 5.2 meters long with a hip height of 2 meters.
facts.quote: Earlier, in 2008, an adult specimen was estimated as having a length of 5.2 m and a height at the hip of 2 m.

facts.statement: Eolambia possessed a crestless skull with a shape similar to those of Equijubus and Probactrosaurus.
facts.quote: The crestless skull of Eolambia has a similar overall shape to those of Equijubus and Probactrosaurus.

facts.statement: The tips of the premaxillae in Eolambia feature two tooth-like denticles, a trait shared with its relative Protohadros.
facts.quote: At the tip of each premaxilla, there are two tooth-like structures known as denticles, which is also seen in its closest relative Protohadros.

facts.statement: A distinguishing characteristic of Eolambia is the concave profile of its maxillary tooth row when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: One of the characteristics used to distinguish Eolambia is the concave profile of the tooth row of the maxilla when viewed from the side

facts.statement: Eolambia had 32 maxillary tooth sockets holding three teeth each and 30 dentary tooth sockets holding four teeth each.
facts.quote: At any given time, each of the 32 maxillary tooth sockets holds three teeth, while each of the 30 dentary tooth sockets holds four teeth.

facts.statement: In Eolambia, two of the teeth in each socket were replacement teeth while the others were active teeth.
facts.quote: Out of these, two of the teeth in each socket are replacement teeth like those of Probactrosaurus; the others are active teeth.

facts.statement: The crowns of Eolambia's teeth bore small, denticle-like serrations on their front and rear edges.
facts.quote: All of the crowns also bear small, denticle-like serrations on the front and rear edges, which is also seen in Probactrosaurus.

facts.statement: Eolambia possesses cervical vertebrae that are very opisthocoelous, with front ends strongly convex and back ends strongly concave.
facts.quote: Like Equijubus, Probactrosaurus, Gongpoquansaurus, and other styracosternans, Eolambia has cervical vertebrae which are very opisthocoelous, meaning that their front ends are strongly convex while their back ends are strongly concave.

facts.statement: The rearmost cervical vertebrae of Eolambia feature a deep depression separating the postzygapophyses and neural spines with steeply-angled front margins that create prominent spike-like projections.
facts.quote: In the rearmost cervicals, there is also a deep depression separating the postzygapophyses, and the neural spines have steeply-angled front margins, which has the effect of creating prominent spike-like projections.

facts.statement: The first few dorsal vertebrae of Eolambia resemble cervical vertebrae but possess taller and more prong-like neural spines.
facts.quote: The first few dorsal vertebrae are similar to the cervical vertebrae, but have taller and more prong-like neural spines.

facts.statement: The remaining dorsal vertebrae of Eolambia are amphiplatyan, meaning they are flat at both ends.
facts.quote: The rest are amphiplatyan, meaning that they are flat at both ends.

facts.statement: The best-preserved sacrum found among Eolambia specimens to date includes seven vertebrae.
facts.quote: Among the Eolambia specimens found to date, the best-preserved sacrum includes seven vertebrae.

facts.statement: Because the specimen with seven sacral vertebrae was immature and hadrosaurs increase their sacral count with age, adult Eolambia likely had more than seven sacrals.
facts.quote: Given that this individual is immature, and hadrosaurs increase their sacral vertebra count with age, adults may have had more sacrals.

facts.statement: The caudal vertebrae of Eolambia are amphicoelous, having both front and back ends that are concave.
facts.quote: The caudal (tail) vertebrae are amphicoelous, having both the front and back ends being concave.

facts.statement: The humerus of Eolambia is bowed towards the midline and features a prominently thickened deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: The humerus is bowed towards the midline, and the deltopectoral crest on the humerus is prominently thickened.

facts.statement: The hand of Eolambia has five digits.
facts.quote: The hand has five digits.

facts.statement: The claw on the first digit of Eolambia is distinctively conical, a trait shared with Iguanodon, Probactrosaurus, and other basal iguanodonts.
facts.quote: Like Iguanodon, Probactrosaurus, and other basal iguanodonts, the claw on the first digit is distinctively conical.

facts.statement: The hip socket of Eolambia is quite large relative to the ilium compared to other iguanodonts.
facts.quote: The hip socket itself is quite large relative to the ilium for an iguanodont.

facts.statement: The foot of Eolambia has four digits.
facts.quote: The foot has four digits.

facts.statement: In its initial description, Eolambia was classified as a member of the Hadrosauridae family.
facts.quote: In Kirkland's initial description of Eolambia, he considered it to be a member of the Hadrosauridae, as defined by David B. Weishampel, David B. Norman, and Dan Grigorescu in 1993.

facts.statement: Kirkland assigned Eolambia to the suborder Euhadrosauria.
facts.quote: Kirkland further assigned Eolambia to the Euhadrosauria

facts.statement: Kirkland debated whether Eolambia was a basal member of the Lambeosaurinae or their sister group.
facts.quote: Within the Hadrosauridae, Kirkland further considered Eolambia to either be a basal member of the Lambeosaurinae, or the sister group of Lambeosaurinae.

facts.statement: Jason Head re-evaluated the classification of Eolambia in 2001 using specimens from the OMNH.
facts.quote: In 2001, Jason Head re-evaluated the phylogenetic position of Eolambia based on specimens stored at the OMNH.

facts.statement: Jason Head concluded that Eolambia belongs to the Hadrosauroidea but is outside the Hadrosauridae family.
facts.quote: Head concluded that Eolambia was a basal member of the Hadrosauroidea, outside of the Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: The parent group of Eolambia is Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hadrosauroidea

facts.statement: Eolambia is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Eolambia lived from the Aptian to the Cenomanian stages, between 121.4 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Cenomanian (121.4 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 12 recorded fossil occurrences of Eolambia in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 12
